title: Kevin's Kenyon Updates: Holden Dinner, Paranormal Researcher, Fruit Sale and more
excerpt: A Flavorful Tradition of More Than 50 Years: Holden All Saints’ Dinner, Nov. 1
content:
A Flavorful Tradition of More Than 50 Years: Holden All Saints’ Dinner, Nov. 1

Holden Lutheran has observed many cherished traditions since 1856. One of them is the annual All Saints’ Dinner, taking place this year on Sunday, Nov. 1. Holden began hosting All Saints’ Dinners in the 1970s.

Dine-in meals are served from noon to 2 p.m. and 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. Takeout is also available. To reserve a takeout meal, email holdendinner@gmail.com or call 507-789-6677. Enjoy meatballs and gravy, pulsa, side dishes and dessert for $20 per meal. Delivery is available upon request. Payment may be made by cash or check payable to Holden WELCA.

Holden’s Stewardship Committee will host a raffle again at the All Saints’ Festival.

Chad Lewis, paranormal researcher

On Thursday, Nov. 5, at 6 p.m., the Kenyon Public Library will host author and paranormal researcher Chad Lewis’ presentation called “Minnesota’s Most Haunted Locations.”

Lewis will lead the audience on a ghostly journey through some of Minnesota’s most haunted places. Traveling across the state, he will share stories of wandering ghosts in the North Woods, a haunted bed and breakfast in Wabasha, phantom creatures prowling the woods and apparitions in graveyards. His stories draw on firsthand accounts from Minnesotans and explore possible origins of the apparitions he describes.

As a researcher and lecturer, Lewis holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in psychology and has spent nearly 30 years traveling the world to study parapsychology, which examines psychic phenomena and other paranormal activities to determine their validity.

Locally, several residences have experienced numerous unexplained occurrences. In the house portion of the old Kenyon Sunset Home, lights turned on and windows opened when the building was empty.

This presentation is recommended for teens and adults.

This project has been funded by the people of Minnesota through the Arts and Cultural Heritage Library Legacy Fund, in cooperation with SELCO, the Southeast Minnesota Regional Library System.

FFA fruit sale

K-W FFA members are accepting orders for their annual fruit sale through Nov. 4.

Items for sale include oranges, clementines, grapefruit and a variety of apples and pears.

Nonfruit items include cheeses and cheese spreads, beef sticks, cashews and gourmet mixed nuts.

To place an order, contact an FFA member or email mschultz@kw.k12.mn.us. The order form may be viewed on the Kenyon-Wanamingo FFA Chapter Facebook page.

VFW Auxiliary National Scholarship Patriotic Art Contest

The Kenyon VFW Auxiliary offers students in grades 9-12 the opportunity to participate in the VFW Auxiliary National Scholarship Young American Creative Patriotic Art Contest. This scholarship contest, which began in 1979, recognizes up-and-coming artists and encourages patriotism in youth.

Entry forms for the Young American Creative Art Contest are available at the Kenyon Public Library.

National Patriotic Art Contest Illustrating America

The VFW Auxiliary’s Illustrating America contest is a national art competition for students in grades K-8. Entries are judged on patriotic themes and artistic technique, and first-place winners in each division receive $100 gift cards.

The Illustrating America contest, organized by the VFW Auxiliary National, introduces, encourages and recognizes young artists through patriotic art. It is open to elementary and middle/junior high school students in grades K-2, 3-5 and 6-8, with separate national awards for first, second and third place in each division.

Official Rules and Entry Forms are available at the Kenyon Library.

Fall sports-KAN

The fall high school sports seasons have moved on to tournament play.

The seventh-seeded K-W football team faced the second-seeded Goodhue on Tuesday night in the opening round of the Section 4 AA tournament.

The football team faced a challenging schedule again this year as the smallest AA school in the Southeast Central Black District. The team played well enough to win a few games, but unfortunately the ball did not bounce their way. While the players are probably disappointed that they did not get a win, K-W fans are proud of how hard they played every game and did not quit until the final whistle.

The K-W volleyball team finished the season as Gopher Conference Champions with a 10-0 conference record. Many players were excited to beat Fillmore Central in a midseason tournament. The game against Triton was especially rewarding because they defeated K-W last season. This year, Triton led 22-17 in one set, but the K-W girls came back to win in overtime and then won the match. The match decided who would finish in first place in the conference.

Even though we attend every K-W game, I often watch them again on the KAN to catch plays I missed and see what Jack Beulke has put together for the extra segments. Jack puts a lot of time and effort into the trivia questions and halftime videos stored in a vault for games.

We are fortunate to have dedicated people who do the production and broadcasting on the KAN. Most schools don’t have a play-by-play broadcast, which makes it hard to know what is happening.

Minnesota football

Late Saturday afternoon, Minnesota defeated Iowa to claim the Floyd of Rosedale trophy. I listened to the first half on my drive home, watched the third quarter, then went to church and missed the final quarter. I deliberately left my phone at home so I would not be tempted to check the score during the service.

After learning the final score, I texted Miriam Stolee Dotson, a devoted Gopher fan, to see if she’d heard from John Brown, an Iowa fan who has an extensive collection of Hawkeye memorabilia.

She responded with, “This morning John was kind enough to send a picture of himself with Floyd. Well, I guess Floyd will be with us for the year, where he belongs.”

Miriam was at church choir practice during the fourth quarter. One choir member, also from Minnesota, was listening to the game. He tapped Miriam on the shoulder when the game was over and gave the thumbs up. She refrained from shouting Hallelujah.

For the first time since 1978, the Little Brown Jug, Paul Bunyan’s Axe and Floyd of Rosedale are all at home in Minnesota.

In the fall of 1977, Minnesota defeated Michigan for the Jug and Wisconsin for the Axe. The following season, the Gophers won Floyd, bringing all three trophies to Minneapolis for two weeks. Then Michigan took the Brown Jug home, and after the final game of the 1978 season, Wisconsin had the Axe.

The planets must have aligned in Minnesota’s favor after the Vikings’ Sunday win. It’s a rare week when Minnesota football fans can spend their time smiling instead of whining.

Kevin Anderson is a guest contributor and columnist for The Kenyon Leader.
